First we get the address info which contains all the necessary details
(family, type, etc..). This is a linked-list from which we can select what we
need. addrinfo contains socketaddr which is complicated. that's why there
are ipv4 and ipv6 versions of this structure which can be casted back to
socketaddr whenever the time is right.
In fact, the entire address can be casted using socketadrr_storage
size_t ai_addrlen; // size of ai_addr in bytes
struct addrinfo *ai_next; // linked list, next node
unsigned short sa_family; // address family, AF_xxx
char sa_data[14]; // 14 bytes of protocol address
short int sin_family; // Address family, AF_INET
unsigned short int sin_port; // Port number
unsigned char sin_zero[8]; // Same size as struct sockaddr
// Internet address (a structure for historical reasons)
uint32_t s_addr; // that's a 32-bit int (4 bytes)

2. recv(): uses a buffer of fixed size; returns the bytes

6. shutdowns: shutdowns further incoming/outgoing reqs. this

Calls such as socket, send, recv, etc. are blocking. It means that will wait/sleep until some data arrives.
The issue is that unnecessary CPU utilization. One can use fcntl to make it non-blocking.
There are some calls which will do a better job where the OS will do the dirty work:
1. poll(): it takes an array of fds struct and a timeout. the struct has 3 fields -- fd, events (to consider), revents
(events which has happened). the events are incoming, outgoing and connection close.
